Context: on the previous page Grothendieck works with presheaves X on the category of finite sets I with card I ≤ 3. Its maps are epis and monos between the standard sets E_1, E_2, E_3, with inclusions ∂_n: E_n→E_{n+1} and surjections k_{n-1}: E_n→E_{n-1}. He lists the elementary commutative squares (I)–(V) relating them. Writing X_n = X(E_n), the data is a 2-truncated *symmetric* simplicial set (indexing by n-element sets, so n points, not [n-1]).

On this page:
(1) Notation. 𝔊_2 = S_2 acts on X_2 and 𝔊_3 = S_3 acts on X_3, with generators ρ (3-cycle) and σ_1, σ_2, σ_3 (transpositions). The face maps are p_0, p_1: X_2→X_1 and p_12, p_23, p_31: X_3→X_2. The degeneracies are δ_0: X_1→X_2 and δ_1, δ_2, δ_3: X_2→X_3.
(2) Surjectivity (Kan-type) conditions:
- (p_0,p_1): X_2→X_1×X_1 is epi (any two 'points' are joined; note p_0σ = p_1).
- X_3→X_2×X_1 (an edge plus a vertex) is epi, and so further to X_1^3.
- X_3→X_2×_{X_1}X_2 via (p_12,p_23) is epi. This is the 2-dimensional horn-filling/composition condition, then mapped further onto X_2×_{X_1}(X_1×X_1).
Because of the symmetric-group actions, all horns are equivalent, so one condition suffices.
(3) 'iso ???'. He asks whether the degeneracy δ_0: X_1→X_2 identifies X_1 with the fibre of X_2→X_1×X_1 over the diagonal. This would be a 'thinness'/reflexive-relation condition.
(4) He translates the elementary squares of finite sets (E_1→E_2⇉E_3, k_2, k_2', k_1, and ∂_1 with ∂_3 or ∂_2) into squares of the X_n. He marks some of these as cartesian ('cart'):
- δ_1, δ_3: X_2→X_3 against δ_0: X_1→X_2;
- p_12 against the degeneracies K_1, K_2'.
These are conditions requiring that degenerate simplices be exactly those whose faces are degenerate in the appropriate way. This is the standard Eilenberg–Zilber-type cartesianness of degeneracy/face squares, here tested in the symmetric setting.
(5) Reduced case (X_1 a point). Then X_2 is a 𝔊_2-set with a marked fixed point δ_2, and X_3 is a 𝔊_3-set with a marked fixed point δ_3, linked by δ_2: X_2→X_3 and K_2: X_3→X_2 with K_2δ_2 = id. These maps are compatible with the group actions and the degeneracies.
(6) The next page tests this on the coskeletal example X_n = X_1^n, with ζ = (x,y) and formulas like dσ(ζ) = (y,x,x).

Purpose: understanding combinatorial (truncated, symmetric) simplicial models — possibly of groupoid/equivalence-relation type — needed for 'topos stratifié'.
errors: The 'iso ???' identification (δ_0 X_1 = fibre of X_2→X_1×X_1 over the diagonal) fails in general. For the nerve of a groupoid, that fibre consists of all automorphisms, so it is an iso only for equivalence-relation-like (thin) objects. Grothendieck's question marks are justified; the page does not resolve it.

Several labels in the diagrams are ambiguous or overwritten (e.g. ∂_2/∂_3, K_1 vs k_1, δ_2 vs δ_0 at the bottom of the cartesian square). The intended indexing of which degeneracy squares are cartesian cannot be fully certified from the page.

ideas.what: Presheaves on finite sets of cardinality ≤3 (epis/monos), i.e. truncated symmetric simplicial sets with S_n-actions on X_n
ideas.modern_name: (truncated) symmetric simplicial sets / presheaves on FinSet_{≤n}
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; studied e.g. by Grandis, Rosický–Tholen; Grothendieck's own Pursuing Stacks touches on variants

ideas.what: Surjectivity of X_2→X_1×X_1 and of X_3→X_2×_{X_1}X_2 (horn filling)
Reduced case X_1=pt: pointed S_2-set and S_3-set with retraction K_2δ_2=id
ideas.modern_name: reduced symmetric simplicial sets / one-object case

deep.surprise_reason: Routine scratch work: Grothendieck sets up face/degeneracy conventions and Kan-type surjectivity and cartesian conditions for truncated symmetric simplicial sets, and tests the reduced case. Nothing goes beyond standard simplicial combinatorics, and the one open question ('iso ???') has a known negative answer in general.
transcription_corrections: Top right: '(p_12, p_3)' likely means the map X_3→X_2×X_1 given by an edge face p_12 and a vertex projection; the second arrow is labelled '(p_0,p_1)×id_{X_1}'.
The crossed-out '[-p = q-]' at top left appears to be a struck-out 'β=1' or similar; it is not the condition p=q.
'p_31' belongs among the arrows X_2⇇X_3 (three face maps p_12, p_23, p_31), not as a separate label.
In the first circled cartesian square, the top arrow is δ_1: X_2→X_3 (drawn as a hooked arrow X_3←X_2), not X_3→X_2.
Bottom left: the arrows are X_1 ⇄ X_2 ⇄ X_3 labelled δ_1^*, K_1^* and δ_2^*, K_2^*. The middle object is X_2 (overwritten), and the first object is X_1 (written like X_φ).
